subject: Sentry streaming SLOs & customer-led loadtest orchestration
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Li <amanda.li@sentry.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Recap + next steps: streaming SLOs and customer-led load test

Amanda — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your customer-led load test scheduled.

Summary (what we heard)
- SLO targets: p95 latency target <= 120ms, p99 <= 280ms for single-turn streaming responses when using our streaming endpoint.
- Throughput target: sustained 750 requests/sec for synchronous endpoints; for streaming use-case you expect ~200 concurrent streams with an average token emission rate of ~30 tokens/sec.
- Concurrency: peak concurrent users ~2,000 across your fleet, but the streaming test will be focused on the 200 concurrent streams profile.
- Failure policy: graceful degradation preferred (fallback to smaller model) rather than hard errors.

What Redwood will provide
- k6 test scenario (attached): a streaming scenario that opens a WebSocket/SSE stream, feeds prompt payloads, and validates continuous token emission and final transcript delivery.
- A short runbook with observability links so Sentry can watch token-level latency and per-route breakdowns in the Redwood Console.
- Temporary test API key / test account for Sentry to use during the window.

What we need from Sentry
- Confirm the test window: proposed slot is Thu 15 Apr 2027 02:00–06:00 UTC (low traffic on your side). If that doesn't work suggest alternatives.
- Provide the public CIDR ranges to allowlist (or confirm you want us to provide ours).
- Confirm whether you will test via WebSocket or Server-Sent Events (SSE) so we run the correct k6 connector.
- If possible, share a small sample of the prompts/streaming length distribution to tune the scenario.

Action items / owners
- Amanda: confirm window and SSE vs WS preference; provide allowlist CIDRs.
- Neha (cc): we will send the test account and pre-provision tokens; Neha will also post the k6 ssh endpoint and creds.
- Marissa: will stand up the Redwood Console trace dashboard and share link ahead of the run.

Attachments: sentry_k6_streaming_scenario_v1.js (k6 script), slo_target_matrix.xlsx (SLO matrix we captured on the call)

If that looks right I can open the HubSpot deal activity and mark this as "customer-led test scheduled" once we confirm the window.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.ai

From: Amanda Li <amanda.li@sentry.io>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Chen <mike.chen@sentry.io>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 01:19:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: streaming SLOs and customer-led load test

Thanks Lauren — this matches our notes. A few clarifications and requests before we lock the window: 

1) Protocol: we prefer WebSockets for this test; our production ingest uses WS and we want the k6 scenario to mirror that.

2) Test window: Thu 15 Apr 2027 02:00–06:00 UTC works for our infra team. Please confirm you have capacity to support that slot.

3) Allowlist: we'll need a list of IPs/CIDRs from Redwood so our security team can pre-authorize them. Can you provide those by EOD tomorrow?

4) Sample prompts: attached is a short file (sent via separate link to our SRE Slack) with typical message sizes; average stream length ~12–18 tokens before a pause, bursts up to 90 tokens. That should be enough to tune emission rate.

Also — can you confirm whether the test can include a short canary phase (10 minutes) at a lower concurrency to validate connectivity before ramping to 200 concurrent streams? We prefer a staged ramp.

Happy to loop in our procurement contact if we need temporary MSA or test-data agreements.

— Amanda
Amanda Li
Senior Engineering Manager, Integrations — Sentry
amanda.li@sentry.io

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: streaming SLOs and customer-led load test

Amanda — thanks, confirmed on our end for Thu 15 Apr 02:00–06:00 UTC. We can do a staged canary phase of 10 minutes at ~20 concurrent streams then ramp to 200.

IP ranges: attaching the CIDR list we will use for the test. Please have your security team add these to your allowlist: sentry_ip_allowlist_cidrs.txt (attached). Note the list contains ephemeral ranges our load harness will originate from and a small set of static egress addresses used by the Redwood control plane.

Test auth: we'll provision a scoped test API key that only allows the streaming test route and will expire after 24 hours. Neha will post the test key and the k6 endpoint details in a follow-up (she's CC'd).

Runbook notes: Marissa will share the Redwood Console dashboard link and a short checklist to validate token-level latency, KV cache hit rates, and any model fallback events. Please let us know which PagerDuty contact to ping if we see regressions during the run.

Attachments: sentry_ip_allowlist_cidrs.txt, sentry_k6_streaming_scenario_v1.js

Next steps:
- Neha: provision test key + post credentials (ASAP).
- Amanda: confirm PagerDuty contact and any procurement ok to proceed (if needed).
- Marissa: share dashboard link and tracing hooks.

— Lauren
